item.title: Details as Elon Musk says Ukraine violated Starlink's terms and conditions
item.description: Ukraine's Starlink defense systems are back to their normal speeds, according to the country's leadership. Elon Musk justified his decision to disrupt Starlink's service in Ukraine, saying its military violated the terms of service. CBS News national security correspondent Charlie D'Agata reports.

item.title: DOJ takes steps to charge James Comey again
item.description: The DOJ took steps to charge James Comey with leaking information earlier this month, in its third attempt to bring criminal charges against the former FBI director and Trump foe.

item.title: Trump encourages Republicans to support down-ballot races
item.description: President Trump visited deep-red Mississippi on Monday, rallying for incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, who is facing off against Democrat Scott Colom. CBS News correspondent Skyler Henry has more from Corinth.

item.title: Court dismisses DOJ's request to force California to set aside ballots
item.description: A federal appeals court on Monday dismissed the DOJ's effort to force California election officials to set aside thousands of ballots that the Trump administration claims may have been cast by alleged noncitizens.

item.title: Extended Interview: Homeland Security's James Percival on third-country deportations
item.description: In an extended interview with 60 Minutes contributor Gianna Toboni, Department of Homeland Security General Counsel James Percival talks about third-country deportations.

item.title: Republican, Democratic strategists break down pre-midterm rhetoric from Trump, Obama
item.description: Republican strategist Erin Maguire and Democratic strategist John McCarthy join "The Takeout" to discuss campaign rhetoric from President Trump and former President Barack Obama ahead of the midterms.

item.title: Does America Need More Police? With Malcolm Gladwell
item.description: Malcolm Gladwell argues that America has been dishonest about gun violence and explains why he believes reducing murders requires more police, not fewer. If you'd like to share your own great question, email us at greatquestion@cbsnews.com.

item.title: Breaking down the legal battle over California's election process
item.description: Over the weekend, Attorney General Todd Blanche insisted on "Face the Nation" that the Department of Justice is not laying the groundwork to overturn unfavorable election results. CBS News election law expert and contributor David Becker has more.

item.title: Rep. Jake Auchincloss says Americans "know who Democrats are against," but not who they're for
item.description: Democrats are starting to plan beyond the midterms, preparing for the 2028 presidential race. There's a moderate group called Majority Democrats that will hold a summit called "What's Next." The group's chair, Rep. Jake Auchincloss of Massachusetts, joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Johnny Garcia, Democrat running for Congress, says Republican voters are "fed up" with GOP policies
item.description: Johnny Garcia, the Democratic candidate for Texas' 35th congressional district, joins "The Takeout" to discuss disaffected Republicans, Hispanic voter frustration and more ahead of the midterms.

item.title: Breaking down how Israel's elections work as Netanyahu faces opposition threat
item.description: On Tuesday, Israel will hold its first parliamentary elections since the Hamas terrorist attacks on Oct. 7, 2023. Israel has been on a war footing ever since. This election is in part a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's aggressive tactics. CBS News chief correspondent Matt Gutman reports.

item.title: DOJ trying to charge Trump-foe James Comey for third time, records show
item.description: The Justice Department is working to bring a third criminal case against former FBI director James Comey, court records show. He said, "I'm still innocent. I'm still not afraid of these people and I still believe in the independent federal judiciary." CBS News legal analyst Jessica Levinson has more.

item.title: Trump stumps for Republicans in deep-red Mississippi
item.description: As gas prices remain essentially the same as during the Biden administration, President Trump is stumping for Republican candidates in deep-red states like Mississippi. CBS News' Weijia Jiang reports on the White House's midterm strategy, and CBS News executive director of elections and surveys Anthony Salvanto has polling.

item.title: Analyzing Democratic, Republican strategies to sway voters
item.description: The countdown to the midterm elections is on, and both sides of the aisle have deployed strategies to appeal to voters. CBS News contributor Chuck Rocha and former RNC spokesperson Kevin Sheridan break down the different approaches.

item.title: Ukraine disputes Elon Musk's claim that drone strikes violated Starlink's terms
item.description: According to SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Ukraine violated Starlink's rules. He said it used the civilian satellite internet network for an offensive drone strike. Ukrainian officials dispute the statement. Clayton Swope, deputy director of the Aerospace Security Project at CSIS, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Trump campaigning in red states to reassure Republican voters
item.description: President Trump will work to court voters for Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi on Monday ahead of the midterms. Skyler Henry has more details.

item.title: Trump, Obama on campaign pushes as Democrats poised to take the House, CBS News poll shows
item.description: President Donald Trump and former President Barack Obama made their rounds across the U.S. ahead of the midterm elections. A new CBS News poll found that Democrats are on track to take control of the House of Representatives. CBS News contributor Kyle Kondik has more.

item.title: Iran shrugs off Trump's attack threats, says diplomacy ongoing
item.description: Iran says indirect negotiations with the U.S. continue but rules out bending to Trump's demands, even if he orders new strikes.

item.title: Is the Federal Reserve likely to raise interest rates this week?
item.description: Fed officials will unveil their latest interest rate move this week, following the September rate hike, the first in three years.

item.title: Bishops lament White House meeting that produced photo with Trump
item.description: Two Catholic bishops have expressed regret about agreeing to a White House meeting that produced a publicly distributed photo of them praying with President Trump.

item.title: Walter Koenig, actor who played Chekov on "Star Trek," dies at 90
item.description: Walter Koenig played Pavel Chekov in the original "Star Trek" television series and several movies.

item.title: Dollar General overcharged people at checkout for years, FTC says
item.description: The discount retailer routinely charges customers more at checkout than the prices it displays on shelves, price tags and ads, according to federal and state authorities.

item.title: Notable Deaths in 2026
item.description: A look back at the esteemed personalities who've left us this year, who'd touched us with their innovation, creativity and humanity.

item.title: Microsoft offers buyouts to 60,000 workers as it invests more in AI
item.description: Roughly a quarter of Microsoft's workforce will be eligible for a "voluntary exit offer" as the company tries to shed workers.

item.title: New poll shows why Democrats, Republicans are voting in the midterm elections
item.description: The midterms are days away, and new polling data suggests voters are heading to the polls over certain issues. CBS News' Fin Gómez, Nancy Cordes and Ed O'Keefe have the latest.

item.title: María Corina Machado is back in Venezuela. What will happen next?
item.description: María Corina Machado is back in Venezuela as demands for a democratic election continue. CBS News' Lilia Luciano reports.

item.title: Maurene Comey, James Comey's daughter, was unlawfully fired, judge rules
item.description: Maurene Comey was abruptly fired in July 2025 from her job as a federal prosecutor in the Southern District of New York. She sued the DOJ over her firing, claiming it was unlawful.

item.title: These factors could decide Netanyahu's fate in Israel's election
item.description: Israelis are about to vote to choose their next government. The race is wide open, and Benjamin Netanyahu's political fate could hinge on a couple key factors.

item.title: Consumers face scarier Halloween costs this year. Here's why.
item.description: Americans are forecast to spend a record $13.5 billion on Halloween this year, with the average consumer shelling out hundreds of dollars.

item.title: Venezuela opposition leader María Corina Machado returns to country
item.description: Machado covertly snuck out of the South American country in December with a private U.S. rescue team to accept the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize in Norway.
